question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨2 x - z,\,y - z,\,y + z⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=3 x + y$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $-1\le y\le 5.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{5}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,3 u + v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 5\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3 u + v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,3⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3 u + v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2 x - z,\,y - z,\,y + z⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=3 u + v} \\  & =⟨2 u - (3 u + v),\,v - (3 u + v),\,v + (3 u + v)⟩ \\  & =⟨- u - v,\,- 3 u,\,3 u + 2 v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨- u - v,\,- 3 u,\,3 u + 2 v⟩\cdot ⟨-3,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(- u - v)\cdot (-3)+(- 3 u)\cdot (-1)+(3 u + 2 v)\cdot (1) \\  & =3 u + 3 v+3 u+3 u + 2 v \\  & =9 u + 5 v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨2 x - z,\,y - z,\,y + z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A. \\  & ={∬}_{D}(9 u + 5 v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{5}(9 u + 5 v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,- uv + u - v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,1\le u\le 5,\,0\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(- uv + u - v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1 - v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(- uv + u - v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,- u - 1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 - v \\ 0 & 1 & - u - 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 - v \\ 1 & - u - 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 - v \\ 0 & - u - 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨v - 1,\,u + 1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z,\,2 xy,\,2 x + 2 y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=- uv + u - v} \\  & =⟨(- uv + u - v),\,2 uv,\,2 u + 2 v⟩ \\  & =⟨- uv + u - v,\,2 uv,\,2 u + 2 v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨- uv + u - v,\,2 uv,\,2 u + 2 v⟩\cdot ⟨v - 1,\,u + 1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(- uv + u - v)\cdot (v - 1)+(2 uv)\cdot (u + 1)+(2 u + 2 v)\cdot (1) \\  & =- uv^{2} + 2 uv - u - v^{2} + v+2 u^{2} v + 2 uv+2 u + 2 v \\  & =2 u^{2} v - uv^{2} + 4 uv + u - v^{2} + 3 v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z,\,2 xy,\,2 x + 2 y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A. \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2 u^{2} v - uv^{2} + 4 uv + u - v^{2} + 3 v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{3}(2 u^{2} v - uv^{2} + 4 uv + u - v^{2} + 3 v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$
